name: Shanghai
title: Ship Thickness Measurement Shanghai | UTM & Hull Gauging
description: UTM Shanghai: ultrasonic thickness gauging of hull structure, tanks and scrubber piping on container ships, bulk carriers and tankers for renewal surveys.
h1: Ship Thickness Measurement and Hull Gauging in Shanghai
intro: Shanghai handles more container traffic than any other port, and its berths at Yangshan and Waigaoqiao see the newest scrubber-fitted tonnage alongside hard-worked feeders, while bulk carriers wait in the Yangtze estuary and ships go into the repair yards upriver. When the only free hours before a survey fall during a Yangshan call, an estuary wait or a docking upriver, that is where the measurements have to be taken. Our technicians travel from India for each job, and the plan is built around the ship's berth schedule rather than ours.

highlights.p: Yangshan and Waigaoqiao berth windows are tight. We fix the list of decks, coamings, piping runs and any tanks that can be certified safe before arrival, so the gauging fits the cargo plan rather than fighting it.

highlights.h: Estuary anchorage as a gauging window
highlights.p: Bulk carriers and tankers waiting in the Yangtze estuary for a berth or river passage can open holds and ballast tanks without losing cargo time — a practical slot for pre-purchase or pre-docking readings.

highlights.h: Data that follows the ship upriver
highlights.p: Readings taken at a Shanghai berth or anchorage are laid out on the class TM report formats, so the yard on the lower Yangtze and the attending surveyor can build on them at the docking.

port.h: Shanghai: the container giant at the mouth of the Yangtze
p: Shanghai is the world's busiest container port, and most of that volume moves through two places: the deep-water terminals at Yangshan, built on islands offshore and linked to the mainland by the Donghai Bridge, and the Waigaoqiao terminals on the south bank of the Yangtze estuary. Mainline services to Europe, the Mediterranean and North America call here alongside a dense network of intra-Asia feeders and Yangtze river shuttles. The result is a port where the largest scrubber-fitted container ships and small, heavily worked feeders lie only a few berths apart, with very different inspection needs.

Container berth stays are short and tightly scheduled, so gauging on a Shanghai call has to be scoped before the ship arrives: which deck, hatch coaming and side-shell areas are reachable with cargo on board, which ballast tanks can be ventilated and certified safe during the stay, and which piping runs can be reached without interfering with cargo operations. Longer windows come from elsewhere in the port system. Bulk carriers and ore carriers often wait at the anchorages in the Yangtze estuary for a berth or for passage upstream, tankers serve the oil and petrochemical terminals around the estuary, and ships heading for repair at yards on the lower Yangtze can be gauged before the steel list is fixed.

What sets Shanghai apart is how much of the decision-making sits in the city itself. Shanghai is a centre for Chinese shipowning, ship leasing and shipping services, so many survey, drydock and sale-and-purchase decisions are taken here even when the ship is somewhere else. Owners buying second-hand tonnage, charterers taking ships on period, lessors receiving a ship back and superintendents preparing for a third or fourth renewal survey all need condition data they can rely on, and a ship calling at Shanghai is often the most convenient place to collect it.

facilities.h: Where hull gauging in Shanghai takes place
p: Most ultrasonic thickness gauging in Shanghai falls into three settings. At the container terminals the work is limited to what can be reached during cargo operations, so it suits weather deck structure, hatch coamings, accommodation and machinery-space piping, and scrubber overboard lines. At anchorage in the estuary, a bulk carrier or tanker in ballast can open tanks and holds, and the team works from a launch arranged by the ship's agent. At a repair yard the whole ship is available, staging and lighting are in place, and gauging can run alongside the class surveyor's close-up survey.

Shanghai's own big shipyards — Jiangnan on Changxing Island, Hudong-Zhonghua and Shanghai Waigaoqiao Shipbuilding — concentrate on newbuilding, so ships trading to Shanghai often dock for repairs elsewhere, further up the Yangtze or in the Zhoushan archipelago to the south. We plan the mobilisation around wherever the ship is actually going to sit still, and keep the measurement plan consistent from pre-docking gauging to the final survey report. Where the next docking is elsewhere in China, the Shanghai readings are handed over with their locations marked on the ship's drawings, so the next yard and surveyor can use them directly.
list: Yangshan Deep-Water Port — mainline container ships during their working time alongside; weather deck, hatch coamings and scrubber overboard lines, reached without disturbing the crane plan.
Waigaoqiao container terminals — gauging on feeders and intra-Asia container ships, where ballast tanks can sometimes be opened during a longer stay.
Yangtze estuary anchorages — bulk carriers, ore carriers and tankers waiting for berths or river passage; hold and tank gauging by launch through the ship's agent.
Oil and petrochemical terminals around the estuary — product and chemical tankers alongside; deck, external shell and piping readings, with tank entry only once gas-free certification allows.
Repair yards on the lower Yangtze — renewal survey gauging, pre-docking steel estimates and re-gauging of renewed plating during drydock periods.
Wusongkou cruise terminal — piping and structural gauging on cruise ships during turnaround calls, scoped around passenger operations and the ship's own maintenance plan.

context.h: Port state control, emission rules and the Shanghai market
p: Shanghai falls under the Tokyo MoU, with port state control carried out by the China Maritime Safety Administration. Inspectors look at structural condition, corrosion in accessible spaces and the state of the fire main and other safety-critical piping, so a superintendent with a doubtful deck area or a wasted fire main is better served gauging and repairing before arrival than explaining it at the gangway. China also applies its own domestic emission control rules in coastal and inland waters, including limits on open-loop scrubber wash-water discharge in some areas, and ships trading between Shanghai and the Yangtze river ports have to plan scrubber operation around them.

That matters for inspection because scrubber wash-water and overboard piping sees heavy, uneven service: long periods in open-loop mode at sea, then closed-loop or idle spells near the coast. Erosion and corrosion in those lines, and at the overboard penetrations in the shell, are a known source of leaks. Shanghai is also a centre of Chinese ship leasing, and a lessor taking a ship back at the end of a bareboat charter needs a condition record as much as an owner buying second-hand. An independent, well-documented thickness survey serves both.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Shanghai
jobs.p: Ship inspection in Shanghai is shaped by short container calls on one side and long estuary waits and yard periods on the other. The jobs below are the kinds of scope superintendents ask for, and each is planned around the ship's actual window — a berth plan, an anchorage notice or a confirmed dock date — with the team mobilised from India once that window is firm enough to apply for visas.
list: Scrubber wash-water and overboard piping on a mainline container ship at Yangshan, gauged during its scheduled time alongside, with the shell penetrations checked from inside the engine room.

Pre-purchase condition gauging of a Capesize or Panamax bulk carrier waiting at the Yangtze estuary anchorage, covering hold frames, hopper tanks, hatch covers and coamings for the buyer's technical team.
Pre-docking gauging of a feeder container ship before it moves to a lower Yangtze repair yard, so the steel renewal estimate and yard specification are ready before the dock date.
Fire main, ballast and sea-water piping gauging on an ageing product tanker at a Shanghai oil terminal ahead of a vetting inspection, focused on lines with a history of pinhole leaks.
Off-hire condition gauging of a ship redelivered in Shanghai at the end of a bareboat charter, giving owner and lessor a shared record of hull and tank condition.

logistics: Most teams land at Shanghai Pudong International Airport; Hongqiao is useful for domestic connections to the upriver yards. Yangshan is reached by road over the Donghai Bridge, and terminal access is through port passes arranged by the ship's agent; anchorage boarding depends on a launch the agent times to the ship's position in the estuary. Technicians travel on Chinese business visas, and the application normally needs an invitation letter from a company in China, so we start the paperwork as soon as the berth, anchorage window or dock date is confirmed rather than waiting for the final ETA.

faqs.q: Can thickness gauging at Yangshan be done during a normal container call?
faqs.a: Yes, within limits. A container ship alongside at Yangshan is working cargo the whole time, so gauging concentrates on what is accessible and safe: weather deck, hatch coamings, accommodation and machinery spaces, and scrubber and sea-water piping. Ballast tanks can be included only if the ship can ventilate and certify them during the stay. We agree that list with the master and superintendent before arrival so nothing depends on improvisation alongside.

faqs.q: Is it better to gauge at anchorage in the Yangtze estuary or at the yard?
faqs.a: It depends on the purpose. For a pre-purchase inspection in Shanghai or a pre-docking steel estimate, a ship in ballast at anchorage gives good access to holds and tanks without using dock time. For renewal-survey gauging that the class surveyor will verify, the yard is usually better, because staging, lighting and cleaning are already in place and the close-up survey happens at the same time.

faqs.q: Do China's domestic emission rules affect scrubber piping inspection in Shanghai?
faqs.a: Indirectly. Where Chinese rules restrict open-loop discharge, ships run closed-loop, switch to compliant fuel or shut the scrubber down, and that idle time is a practical window to gauge wash-water and overboard lines. We take the ship's scrubber operating pattern into account when choosing measurement points, because erosion and corrosion concentrate where flow direction, velocity and water chemistry change.

faqs.q: How far ahead should we contact you for a Shanghai job?
faqs.a: The moment the window is known. The team travels from India, and a Chinese business visa needs an invitation letter and processing time, so a dock date or charter redelivery confirmed some weeks ahead is comfortable. Short-notice berth calls are harder; for those we discuss with the superintendent whether the gauging can move to the next suitable call or to the next yard stay.
